definition: Semantic folding theory describes a procedure for encoding the semantics of natural language text in a semantically grounded binary representation.
details: This approach provides a framework for modelling how language data is processed by the neocortex.

explainer.lead: Semantic folding is a procedure for encoding the semantics of natural language text into a semantically grounded binary representation. It matters as a framework for modelling how language data might be processed by the neocortex.

tiers.eli5: It turns the meaning of text into a pattern of ones and zeros, the way a brain might encode what words mean.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to convert text into binary semantic representations that grounded models can operate on. The pitfall is treating the binary encoding as neutral data when it is tied to a specific theory of how the neocortex processes language.
tiers.paperLevel: Semantic folding theory describes a procedure that encodes natural-language semantics in a semantically grounded binary representation, providing a framework for modelling neocortical processing of language data. Its limits follow from being a theory-driven model of cortical processing rather than a general-purpose encoding.

explainer.example: A passage of natural language text is run through the folding procedure and comes out as a binary representation that carries its semantics in grounded form.
